items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: I'll tell you the man I first seen when I was kind of getting on my feet with Trumpet, the first man I seen, I ain't gonna lie, it was Bunk Johnson.

ctx.x: You wouldn't know my band might go there.

No. I didn't never get to see him. I don't mean I wasn't old enough to see him, but I just never, I'll tell you the man I first seen when I was kind of getting on my feet with Trumpet, the first man I seen, I ain't gonna lie, it was Bunk Johnson. I seen him on my excursion pass our home recently, going to Homer, Louisiana, and I went on that excursion and I saw him play. First time. And I didn't ever see Joe Oliver until I went to Chicago.
That's a funny thing, you can live in the same town with people and never hear him.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: First time I was a young kid, then saw him play and he used to do that, but Bunk held his horn steady.

ctx.x: But, uh, a fellow like Bunk, I don't know, I went on an excursion one time. First time I was a young kid, then saw him play and he used to do that, but Bunk held his horn steady. And he made all kind of different ways on the song, different songs on his horn.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: That's the first time I've seen a bunker.

ctx.x: I didn't know them. That's the first time I've seen a bunker. I was in the country then. I was a little boy then, but I was playing music. And I went on Excursion to home in Louisiana and I stood by a bunker all day long, man. That's not even blow.
Who was he playing with? His own band? Yeah, his own band, yeah.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1958-05-24
items.q: Yeah. I didn't know him that good, but I heard him on excursions after excursions.

ctx.x: Yeah. I didn't know him that good, but I heard him on excursions after excursions.
